answer: Stake-weighted quorum with slashing makes identity costly: each agent locks tokens in a registered vault, and only bonded capital counts toward votes or payouts. A hollow key with no stake has zero weight, so minting thousands buys nothing. To reach the summit of a decision, an attacker must out-stake honest holders, paying a linear capital cost that stays locked while misconduct is checked. Rewards follow one auditable stake thread per agent, so splitting into aliases cannot multiply a share, and double-voting slashes the whole bond, making the attack self-defeating.
